meta.title: Starter Shifter — Client Onboarding Questionnaire
meta.source: Bootstrap snapshot only; live questionnaires are stored in Convex questionnaireVersions
meta.note: This is the complete question library, not one client’s mandatory form. Core topics are shared; service modules are conditional. Optional answers can be skipped. Options are stable saved values; optionLabels and optionDescriptions provide client-friendly presentation. Help explains how to answer; why explains the decision the answer supports.

core.title: Let's meet

questions.label: What name should we use for you?
questions.help: Use the name you normally use at work.
questions.why: This helps us address you correctly in project conversations.

questions.label: What is your business or brand called?
questions.help: Use your public name; your legal billing name comes later.
questions.why: We use this name in the brief and check it against your website and profiles.

questions.label: Which email should we use for this project?
questions.help: Use an inbox you check regularly; a personal email is fine.
questions.why: We use this address for project updates and questions that need your input.

questions.label: What phone number should we use, if needed?
questions.help: Include the country code, for example +91; needed for phone or WhatsApp contact.
questions.why: A reachable number lets us use a phone-based channel if you choose one.

core.description: Tell us who you are and the name we should use for your project.

core.title: How we should work with you

questions.label: What is your role in this project?
questions.help: Choose the role that best describes your involvement.
questions.why: This helps us involve the right people in decisions; we ask about final approval separately.

optionLabels.Authorized representative: Working on behalf of the business

questions.label: Which country and time zone do you work in?
questions.help: Check the suggested time zone; no home address is needed.
questions.why: We use this to arrange reviews at suitable times.

questions.label: How would you like to hear from us?
questions.help: Choose your preferred channels; add a language or contact window in a note.
questions.why: We will confirm the channels we can support and use your preferences to plan communication.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Your business at a glance

questions.label: What does your business do?
questions.placeholder: We sell refillable skincare to customers in India through our store and Instagram.
questions.help: In two or three sentences, tell us what you sell, who it helps, and how.
questions.why: This becomes the starting point for research, website content, and marketing direction.

questions.label: Which industry are you in?
questions.help: Choose the closest match; add your niche if the categories are too broad.
questions.why: Your industry helps us find relevant competitors and spot requirements to investigate.

questions.label: Which description best fits your business today?
questions.help: Choose your current situation, rather than where you hope to be.
questions.why: We adapt recommendations to what already exists and what still needs to be built.

optionLabels.Already online: We sell online and want to improve
optionLabels.Expanding or improving: We are expanding into new markets or channels
optionLabels.Established internal team: This project is for our internal team

optionDescriptions.Already online: Improving your current online experience is the main goal.
optionDescriptions.Expanding or improving: Adding markets, channels, or a new line of business is the main goal.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: What you offer

questions.label: What will this project help you sell or deliver?
questions.help: Choose every business model that applies to this project.
questions.why: Your choices reveal relevant follow-up questions, such as delivery, bookings, or subscriptions.

optionLabels.Marketplace connecting buyers and provid: A marketplace for buyers and sellers
optionLabels.Not decided: Help me choose a business model

questions.label: Which products or services should we focus on first?
questions.help: Add up to three examples, with a catalog link if you have one.
questions.why: These examples help us plan the first launch around the offers that matter most.

questions.label: Where do you sell now, and where would you like to sell next?

fields.label: Current markets
fields.placeholder: For example: India, mainly Mumbai and Pune

fields.label: Planned markets
fields.placeholder: For example: UAE next year, or not decided

questions.help: Name cities, regions, or countries; planned expansion can be undecided.
questions.why: Markets affect language, currency, delivery, research, and the requirements we must verify.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Who this is for

questions.label: Who is your main customer or user?
questions.help: Describe their need, location, and buying situation; one useful group is enough.
questions.why: We use this to shape navigation, product information, and marketing messages for the right people.

questions.label: Does the person using your product also choose and pay for it?
questions.help: If not, add the roles involved, such as a parent, manager, or purchasing team.
questions.why: Different buyers and users may need different information, approvals, or account access.

optionLabels.Different people: Different people decide, pay, or use it
optionLabels.No payment involved: There is no payment in this process

questions.label: What helps a customer decide to buy from you?
questions.help: Use one example of their need, concern, and reason for choosing or leaving.
questions.why: Customer concerns guide product pages, FAQs, trust information, and follow-up messages.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Why you are starting this project

questions.label: What made you start this project now?
questions.help: Describe the main problem, opportunity, or change behind this decision.
questions.why: This tells us what needs attention first and what would make the project useful.

questions.label: What are the three most important improvements you want?
questions.help: Choose up to three, then mark the one that matters most.
questions.why: Your priority helps us make trade-offs when time, budget, or capacity is limited.

optionLabels.Online presence: Help people find and understand us
optionLabels.Customer experience: Make buying or getting help easier
optionLabels.Staff adoption: Help our team use the new process

questions.label: What outcome would make this project worthwhile?
presets: Help us set a realistic target
questions.help: Name a result and review date, or ask us to help set a target.
questions.why: We compare this goal with your starting point before agreeing realistic success measures.

questions.label: What starting numbers do you have for your main goal?
questions.help: Share one recent result with its date range and source; estimates are fine.
questions.why: A starting point lets us compare progress fairly. Revenue is optional; a new business can say it has not launched.
questions.placeholder: About 120 orders in October, from our store report; estimated.
presets: We do not measure this yet

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: How things work today

questions.label: Which websites and public profiles belong to your business?
questions.help: Add full links to your store, app, social pages, marketplaces, and review listings.
questions.why: We use these sources to research your business and check consistency. Note which links are current; private reports can be shared through agreed access later.

questions.label: How does a typical order or request move through your business?
questions.placeholder: Instagram message → WhatsApp order → payment link → spreadsheet → courier → follow-up
questions.help: Describe one journey from first contact to delivery and follow-up.
questions.why: We map the handoffs between people and tools before proposing changes. A new business can describe its intended process.

questions.label: Where does that process get stuck or create extra work?
questions.help: Give one example, including how often it happens or the time lost if known.
questions.why: This helps us prioritize the cause of a problem and preserve the parts that already work.

questions.label: Which tools does your team use to run the business?
questions.help: Name tools for sales, stock, delivery, accounting, support, and marketing.
questions.why: We look for existing tools to retain and gaps between them before recommending new software.
questions.placeholder: For example: Shopify for orders; a spreadsheet for stock

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: What you want help with

questions.label: What would you like our help with?
questions.help: Choose the areas you need help with; you do not need to know the solution.
questions.why: We show relevant follow-ups and review requests against your agreement. Choices do not change your plan or price; Basic setup and Pro ongoing work have different boundaries.

optionLabels.ERP/CRM or other connections: Connect sales, stock, or business tools

optionDescriptions.Research/design: Understand your market and plan the customer experience.
optionDescriptions.Website/store/application: Build or improve where customers browse, buy, or get help.
optionDescriptions.SEO and search visibility: Help people find your business through search.
optionDescriptions.Email and WhatsApp marketing: Plan messages, signup forms, and customer follow-up.
optionDescriptions.Social presence: Set up or improve your public social profiles and content direction.
optionDescriptions.Campaigns/lead generation: Plan promotions and acquisition; ongoing work depends on your plan.
optionDescriptions.ERP/CRM or other connections: Move information between the tools your team uses.
optionDescriptions.Help me choose: We will recommend priorities from the context you provide.

questions.label: What should customers or staff be able to do?
questions.help: Choose the actions needed at launch, rather than every possible future feature.
questions.why: These actions help us define the pages, steps, and connections the first version needs.

optionLabels.Learn/contact: Learn about us or contact us
optionLabels.Register/sign in: Create an account or sign in
optionLabels.Need guidance: Help me choose the main actions

questions.label: What is essential for launch, and what can wait?
questions.help: List up to three launch priorities, then add later ideas separately.
questions.why: This keeps the first release focused. Add anything explicitly excluded so we can record that boundary.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Your market and reasons to choose you

questions.label: What alternatives do your customers compare you with?
questions.help: Add up to three competitor names or links; offline alternatives count too.
questions.why: We compare offers, buying experiences, and messaging to find useful differences, rather than copy competitors.

questions.label: Why do customers choose you?
questions.help: Separate strengths you can demonstrate today from ideas you want to develop.
questions.why: We use supported differences in positioning and content; planned strengths need validation first.

questions.label: What sources could help us understand your customers and market?
questions.help: Link reviews, research, seasonal demand, or redacted feedback; add the source and date.
questions.why: Evidence helps us check assumptions. Public marketing use of reviews, images, or testimonials needs separate permission.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Brand and content readiness

questions.label: Which brand and content materials do you have?
questions.help: For each relevant item, choose ready, needs updating, or need help.
questions.why: This shows what we can reuse and what may delay delivery. File production and licensing must match the agreed scope.

questions.label: How should your brand look and sound?
questions.help: Choose up to three qualities; add a reference link and what you like about it.
questions.why: We use this to guide design and writing consistently. Add styles or language to avoid.

questions.label: Who can provide and approve your content?
questions.help: Name a person or role, or reuse your project contact.
questions.why: We need a clear owner for product details, photos, copy, and approvals so missing content does not stall the build.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Requirements we should know early

questions.label: Are there restrictions or approvals we should know about?
questions.help: Choose what applies; a brief explanation is enough.
questions.why: We flag requirements that may affect sales, advertising, or launch for review with the responsible person.

questions.label: What private information or account permissions will the project involve?
questions.help: Choose categories only; never paste customer or employee records.
questions.why: This helps us plan access and identify information-handling requirements to verify before implementation.

questions.label: What language or access needs should we plan for?
questions.help: Choose known needs; add specific languages, devices, or barriers in a note.
questions.why: These inputs guide accessible design, translations, and mobile or slow-connection priorities.

optionLabels.Assistive technology: Screen readers or other access tools
optionLabels.Low digital confidence: Customers or staff who need simpler steps

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Timing and practical limits

questions.label: Is there a launch date or event we should plan around?
questions.help: Choose a date, flexible, or not decided; add the reason if the date is fixed.
questions.why: We use this to discuss dependencies and a realistic schedule; entering a date does not confirm it.

questions.label: What budget limits should guide our recommendations?
questions.help: Use a currency and ranges; separate setup, monthly tools/support, and monthly ads.
questions.why: We use these limits to compare options. Your agreement sets agency fees; hosting, domains, ad spend, and other third-party charges are client-paid.

questions.label: What could delay the work or your feedback?
questions.help: Choose known constraints, such as content, access, staffing, or approvals.
questions.why: We can plan around dependencies early instead of discovering them close to launch.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Decisions, reviews, and handover

questions.label: Who has final approval for the project?
questions.help: Use your project contact, or name the approver for scope, design, content, and launch.
questions.why: A clear decision owner helps avoid conflicting feedback; list separate approvers only where needed.

questions.label: Who else should review the research and design?
questions.help: Name people or roles and who will combine their feedback.
questions.why: This helps us plan reviews and hear from the people who will use or run the result.

questions.label: Who will run things after launch?
questions.help: Choose the responsible team; add training or handover needs in a note.
questions.why: We plan ownership and handover around the agreed coverage. Selecting the agency does not add ongoing services.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Your engagement details

questions.label: Does the recorded project agreement look right?
questions.help: Compare the scope, fees, currency, exclusions, and third-party costs with your agreement.
questions.why: We flag differences for review. This answer does not sign a contract or verify a payment.

questions.label: Which legal name and email should appear on your invoices?
questions.help: Confirm the suggested details, or correct them.
questions.why: These details support contracting and billing. Address and tax details are requested separately only when needed.

questions.label: Do you need help with the agreement or advance payment?
questions.help: Describe the blocker without entering payment-card or bank details.
questions.why: We can resolve administrative issues; verified contract and 40% advance status come from agency records.

core.description: Your approved proposal and contract provide the project summary. Selecting work in this form does not create an agreement or verify a payment.

core.title: Your workspace and remaining inputs

questions.label: Which email should have access to your client workspace?
questions.help: Keep your project email or enter a different address you control.
questions.why: The address must be verified before access is granted; this form does not grant permissions.

questions.label: Who else should join your project workspace or group?
questions.help: Add each person’s name, work email, role, and requested access.
questions.why: This records your access request so we can check responsibilities before sending any invitations.

questions.label: How would you like to share remaining files or account access?
questions.help: Choose a sharing method; never enter passwords, one-time codes, or API keys.
questions.why: We will arrange the appropriate sharing or role-based access process for the outstanding items.

core.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

core.title: Review and submit

questions.label: How satisfied are you with this onboarding so far?
questions.help: Choose a rating if you wish; an honest answer will not affect your project.
questions.why: Your feedback helps us improve onboarding. This is an optional experience rating, not approval of scope or a satisfaction guarantee.

questions.label: What would make this onboarding easier?
questions.help: Mention a question, missing choice, or step that felt confusing or unnecessary.
questions.why: We review this alongside your rating to decide what to change. Please leave out private customer details.

questions.label: What else should we understand about your business or project?
questions.help: Add an important concern, missing requirement, or correction.
questions.why: This catches context that did not fit earlier questions before we review the brief with you.

questions.label: Are these details accurate, and are you allowed to share them?
questions.help: Review your answers; keep estimates and unknowns clearly marked.
questions.why: Your confirmation helps us distinguish supplied facts from research still needed. It does not approve project scope.

questions.label: Have you read how we use your onboarding information?
questions.help: Read the onboarding privacy notice before confirming.
questions.why: This acknowledgement covers project use of your information. Marketing permission is separate and is not required for workspace access.

core.description: Check your business, goals, selected work, responsibilities, and open items. You can edit each section before submitting. Submission saves your answers; workspace activation follows verified project prerequisites.

modules.title: Your website's job

questions.label: Are we building a new site or changing an existing one?
questions.help: Choose the closest match; we will reuse the links you already shared.
questions.why: A new build, improvement, or replacement needs a different plan for content, access, and continuity.

questions.label: What do visitors need before they can take the main action?
questions.help: Choose the information or tools that help them decide and continue.
questions.why: This shapes page content and navigation around the customer’s task.

questions.label: Is there a website platform we should use or keep?
questions.help: Choose a preference, or ask for a recommendation; add the current plan if known.
questions.why: We check fit, existing investments, and platform limits before recommending a solution.

questions.label: Which task is hardest for customers on your current site?
questions.help: Give one example or page link, including the device if known.
questions.why: A real problem helps us prioritize the redesign and define a task to check before launch.

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Website ownership and content

questions.label: Who controls your domain, website, and hosting accounts?
questions.help: Name the provider and owner if known; do not share login details.
questions.why: Account ownership and access can affect setup, migration, and handover.

optionLabels.Owned and accessible: We own the accounts and can access them
optionLabels.Owned but access uncertain: We own them but need to check access

questions.label: Which pages or content need to be ready for launch?
questions.placeholder: For example: Home — ready, Services — needs writing
questions.help: List priorities or link an existing page list; mark content ready or needing work.
questions.why: This defines the launch content and who needs to prepare it.

questions.label: What should we keep from your current website?
questions.help: Choose what matters; add important URLs or connections in a note.
questions.why: We identify migration needs and protect useful content, search visibility, and customer access.

optionLabels.URLs/search traffic: Important page links and search visibility

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Product catalog

questions.label: How large is your first product catalog?
questions.help: Choose a band for products; note the separate variation count if known.
questions.why: Ten products with many sizes can involve more setup than ten simple items; rough counts help estimate the work.

questions.label: What choices must a customer make for a product?
questions.help: Choose what applies, then add one example if helpful.
questions.why: Product choices affect the catalog structure, pricing, fulfillment, and checkout.

optionLabels.Nothing: No choices beyond the product itself

optionDescriptions.Variant: For example, a shirt available in several sizes and colors.
optionDescriptions.Text/image personalization: For example, a name or uploaded design printed on a product.

questions.label: Where are your product details, prices, and images kept?
questions.help: Name the tool or link a catalog; a small redacted example is enough.
questions.why: We check data readiness, missing details, image rights, and import needs before building the catalog.

questions.label: Which products matter most commercially?
questions.help: Name best sellers or priorities; share price ranges and margin limits only if comfortable.
questions.why: This helps us prioritize products and avoid promotions that are unsuitable for your costs or supply.

questions.label: How should customers find the right product?
questions.help: Choose useful browsing methods; add important product facts in a note.
questions.why: Your catalog structure and search filters should reflect how people choose, not just how stock is stored.
options: Search by name or product code
Filter by size, color, or material

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Stock and availability

questions.label: Where do you keep stock counts today?
questions.help: Choose the main source; add its name and who updates it.
questions.why: We need a trusted stock source before designing synchronization or availability rules.

optionLabels.Not tracked: We do not track stock yet

questions.label: Which locations and sales channels use the same stock?
questions.placeholder: For example: 2 stores and an online shop
questions.help: List your main warehouses, stores, website, and marketplaces.
questions.why: Shared stock needs rules to reduce overselling; note batches, expiry, or serial numbers only if relevant.

questions.label: What should happen when an item is unavailable?
questions.help: Choose the behaviors you need; add an exception owner if known.
questions.why: We use this to plan availability messages, backorders, and staff checks.

optionLabels.Stop sales: Show sold out and stop orders

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Delivery, pickup, and returns

questions.label: How will orders reach customers?
questions.help: Choose delivery methods; add countries or regions you serve and any exclusions.
questions.why: Delivery methods and areas determine the shipping and pickup choices customers see.

questions.label: What delivery providers and rules do you use?
questions.help: Link your rules or name providers, charges, processing times, and tracking needs.
questions.why: We use these details to check checkout rates and fulfillment connections, including packaging or cross-border constraints.

questions.label: Who handles delivery issues, returns, and refunds?
questions.help: Name the team and link or summarize your returns policy.
questions.why: Clear ownership and rules help us plan customer messages and exception handling; include return costs if known.

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Supplier-made or personalized products

questions.label: Who makes or dispatches your supplier-made products?
questions.placeholder: Supplier or production team — name or link
questions.help: Name suppliers or your production team; label undecided suppliers as options.
questions.why: We need to verify production and dispatch capabilities before connecting the order flow.

questions.label: What needs approval before production starts?
questions.help: Choose the checks needed before an order is made.
questions.why: These checks can prevent incorrect or unapproved orders reaching production; note whether samples and timing are tested.

questions.label: How do you handle supplier failures and supplier payments?
questions.help: Give the responsible person and key remake, deadline, or payment rules.
questions.why: Supplier timing and upfront costs may affect promises, order status, and cash flow.

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Bookings and appointments

questions.label: What can customers book?
questions.placeholder: For example: 30-minute online consultations with one adviser
questions.help: Give one service example with duration, location, staff, and capacity if known.
questions.why: These limits determine available time slots and booking rules.

questions.label: How should a booking be confirmed?
questions.help: Choose the main approach; add your calendar tool if you have one.
questions.why: This determines when we reserve capacity and notify the customer.

questions.label: What are your rescheduling, cancellation, and no-show rules?
questions.help: Link a policy or summarize it; mention deposits and reminders if relevant.
questions.why: We need these rules for booking messages, payment requirements, and changes to availability.

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Quotes, projects, and B2B buying

questions.label: What do you need to know before accepting an inquiry?
questions.help: Choose the details that help you assess fit.
questions.why: We keep inquiry forms focused on information your team actually uses.

questions.label: How does an inquiry become an approved order?
questions.help: Describe the steps or link a quote or order template.
questions.why: Quotes, purchase orders, approvals, and handoffs shape the sales workflow.

questions.label: Do business customers have special buying rules?
questions.help: Choose existing rules such as trade pricing, minimum quantities, or payment terms.
questions.why: These rules may require different accounts, prices, approvals, or checkout behavior.

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Digital products and learning

questions.label: How will customers receive your digital content?
questions.help: Choose delivery methods; add the file or content format if known.
questions.why: Delivery format affects hosting, access, and purchase confirmation.

questions.label: What limits access to the digital content?
questions.help: Choose relevant limits and add any known duration, seat, or license rules.
questions.why: We use these rules to plan who gets access and when it ends.

questions.label: What support or features are needed after access starts?
questions.help: Choose only what your offer needs.
questions.why: Learning, updates, support, and expiry require different follow-up workflows.

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Subscriptions and memberships

questions.label: What does a subscription or membership include?
questions.help: Summarize the ongoing benefit; link existing tiers and billing periods if available.
questions.why: The recurring offer determines delivery, access, and billing requirements.

questions.label: Which subscription billing behaviors do you need?
questions.help: Choose trial, renewal, plan-change, and failed-payment behaviors to discuss.
questions.why: We check these against your policies and provider capabilities before implementation.

questions.label: What happens when a customer pauses or cancels?
questions.help: Link your rules or explain when access or deliveries end and whether refunds apply.
questions.why: Cancellation behavior affects billing, fulfillment, and customer messages.

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Marketplaces and multiple providers

questions.label: Which groups will use the marketplace?
questions.help: Choose the groups and add the main task each needs to do.
questions.why: Each group may need different permissions and screens.

questions.label: How are providers approved and assigned work or orders?
questions.help: Describe selection, quality checks, and who supplies or performs the work.
questions.why: This defines onboarding, matching, and operational responsibilities.

questions.label: Who collects money, pays providers, and resolves disputes?
questions.help: Describe commissions, payouts, refunds, and ownership where relevant.
questions.why: The money flow affects provider feasibility and responsibilities that need specialist review.

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Internal team workflows

questions.label: Which repeated team task should we improve first?
questions.help: Reuse your earlier workflow; add frequency or time spent if known.
presets: Help us choose the priority task
questions.why: We choose a useful first improvement and a baseline for checking its effect.

questions.label: Which team roles need to submit, approve, edit, or view work?
questions.help: Choose roles and explain what each can do.
questions.why: Permissions and approval steps need to reflect how the team actually works.

questions.label: What would help your team use the new process?
questions.help: Choose support such as training, mobile access, or a gradual rollout.
questions.why: A workable rollout matters as much as the tool itself for team adoption.

optionLabels.Parallel running: Keep the old process during a trial

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Customer payments and invoicing

questions.label: How should customers pay you?
questions.help: Choose methods; add customer currencies in a note.
questions.why: This concerns customer payments, separate from your agency fees, and helps us check provider coverage.

optionLabels.Online payment: Online card, wallet, or local payment

questions.label: Which payment and accounting providers do you use?
questions.help: Name providers and whether accounts are approved; never share bank or card credentials.
questions.why: Provider readiness and supported connections affect payment setup and reconciliation.

questions.label: Which approved pricing, tax, invoice, and refund rules apply?
questions.help: Link the rules or name the person who will confirm them.
questions.why: Checkout and invoices must reflect approved business rules; we do not infer tax treatment from a country alone.

questions.label: What does your customer need at checkout?
questions.help: Choose business needs; we will check platform and payment-provider support.
questions.why: Checkout requirements affect conversion, account design, and the steps we need to test before launch.
options: Add a discount or gift card

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Your social presence

questions.label: Which social channels matter most for this project?
questions.help: Choose up to three; reuse earlier profile links and note any missing access.
questions.why: We focus setup or improvements on relevant channels and verify account ownership separately.

questions.label: What should social content help customers do?
questions.help: Choose the main actions or messages to support.
questions.why: This connects content choices to business goals rather than posting without a purpose.

optionLabels.Inquire: Ask about a purchase or service

questions.label: Who will create, approve, and publish social content?
questions.help: Choose the working arrangement; add available formats or capacity in a note.
questions.why: We plan responsibilities and approvals around the agreement; ongoing production needs defined coverage.

optionLabels.Shared: Our team and Starter Shifter together

questions.label: Which social content has brought useful results?
questions.help: Link one useful post or redacted report and say what happened and when.
questions.why: We distinguish attention from inquiries or sales and learn which topics and formats are worth testing.

modules.description: Answer what you know. Estimates are welcome; you can ask for help or return later.

modules.title: Campaign and growth priorities

questions.label: Which offer and audience should marketing focus on first?
questions.help: Build on your earlier answers; name the first offer and customer group.
presets: Help us choose the campaign priority
questions.why: A clear starting point helps us connect campaigns, landing pages, and follow-up.

questions.label: How do customers currently find you?
questions.help: Choose current sources; add one thing that worked or failed with a dated results link.
questions.why: We use past evidence to decide what to retain, test, or investigate rather than guess channel performance.

optionLabels.No history: We have not started marketing yet

questions.label: What spending and promotion limits should marketing follow?
questions.help: Confirm the monthly ad budget already shared; add only promotion limits or changes.
presets: Use the advertising budget already shared
questions.why: We reuse your project budget and check commercial limits. Ad spend is client-paid; requests do not authorize campaign spending.

questions.label: Which searches should help people find your business?
questions.help: Give a few phrases a customer might use, or link important search pages.
questions.why: We use your language as a research starting point, then verify search demand and intent; rankings are not guaranteed.

questions.label: Which marketing accounts and materials can we build on?
questions.help: Name tools or assets and who manages them; add access status without logins.
questions.why: We check analytics, search, ads, email, and creative readiness before planning connections or campaigns.
questions.placeholder: For example: Google Search Console — our team owns it; access needs checking

modules.title: Lead follow-up and repeat business

questions.label: What makes an inquiry a good fit for your business?
questions.help: Choose criteria and add any customers or requests you cannot serve.
questions.why: We use this to distinguish useful inquiries from volume alone.

optionLabels.Need: A need we can help with

questions.label: Who follows up when a new inquiry arrives?
questions.help: Name the owner, destination tool, usual response time, and daily capacity.
questions.why: A campaign needs a workable handoff so inquiries receive timely follow-up.

questions.label: What encourages customers to buy or use your service again?
questions.help: Describe repeat needs, offers, or reasons people stop returning.
presets: Help us identify a repeat offer
questions.why: We use this to plan useful retention messages rather than send promotions without a reason.

questions.label: How have people agreed to receive your marketing messages?
questions.help: Describe signup sources, channels, and where preferences or opt-outs are recorded.
questions.why: We need to verify permissions and channel requirements before using a list. Do not upload subscriber details here.

questions.label: Which customer messages would be most useful?
questions.help: Choose up to three priorities based on customer needs.
questions.why: We use this to plan email or messaging flows, timing, and ownership; implementation depends on scope and verified permissions.

modules.title: Human customer handling

questions.label: Where do customer questions arrive?
questions.help: Choose channels; add rough weekly volume and common topics if known.
questions.why: Volume and channel mix help define staffing, coverage, and workflow needs.

questions.label: Which conversations should the agency help handle?
questions.help: Choose tasks and note what needs your approval.
questions.why: We clarify responsibilities and authority limits against the agreed scope before handling customers.

optionLabels.Qualifying inquiries: Checking whether inquiries are a good fit

questions.label: Who takes over urgent or unresolved customer issues?
questions.help: Name a person or role and their availability.
questions.why: We need a clear escalation path for complaints, sensitive issues, and exceptions; no coverage hours are assumed.

modules.title: Chatbot purpose and knowledge

questions.label: Where should the chatbot help customers?
questions.help: Choose channels and add up to three priority questions or tasks.
questions.why: We check channel capabilities and access before agreeing what the chatbot can do.

questions.label: Which approved information can the chatbot use?
questions.help: Link FAQs, policies, or catalog pages and name who keeps them updated.
questions.why: Reliable sources reduce unsupported answers; private datasets should use an agreed secure process.

questions.label: What language and tone should the chatbot use?
options: Use the language and tone already shared
questions.help: Reuse earlier brand preferences unless customer conversations need something different.
questions.why: This keeps chatbot responses consistent with your brand and customers’ language needs.
exclusiveOptions: Use the language and tone already shared

questions.label: What is the chatbot’s main job?
questions.help: Choose the main job; add other requested actions in a note.
questions.why: Action-taking needs verified access and feasibility checks before it enters the scope.

optionLabels.Collect inquiries: Collect details for a person to follow up
optionLabels.Check status: Look up an order or request status

questions.label: What should always need a person’s approval?
questions.help: Choose decisions or situations the chatbot should not handle on its own.
questions.why: We use these boundaries to define permissions and human review.

questions.label: When should the chatbot hand a conversation to a person?
questions.help: Choose handoff situations and name the receiving team in a note.
questions.why: We plan escalation and what happens when staff are unavailable; add any usage-cost limit if known.

questions.placeholder: When a quote is accepted, create an invoice.
questions.help: Start with one task from the workflow you already described.
presets: Help us choose the first automation
questions.why: A focused first automation makes it easier to verify value and avoid automating a broken process.

questions.label: Which tools need to work together?
questions.help: Choose tool types and add product names or plans if known.
questions.why: We verify connectors, permissions, and platform limits before promising a connection.

questions.label: What starts the automation, and what should happen next?

fields.label: When this happens
fields.placeholder: For example: A quote is accepted

questions.help: Give one trigger and one expected result in everyday words.
questions.why: This defines the first workflow to validate; add frequency or volume only if known.

modules.title: Data rules and failed workflows

questions.label: What information should move between tools?
questions.help: Choose records; add timing and whether information moves one way or both.
questions.why: Record types, direction, and timing determine connection requirements.

questions.label: Which tool has the correct record when tools disagree?
questions.help: Name the trusted source for customers, orders, stock, or invoices where relevant.
questions.why: A trusted source prevents updates from overwriting the wrong information.

questions.label: What should happen if the connection fails?
questions.help: Name the alert recipient and how staff can continue manually.
questions.why: We plan recovery and exception handling alongside the normal workflow.

modules.title: Moving existing data or systems

questions.label: What needs to move from your old tools or website?
questions.help: Choose the information; name each source and rough volume if known.
questions.why: We assess export access, migration work, and what needs verification before moving live data.

questions.label: What problems are already present in that information?
questions.help: Choose known issues and name who can approve cleanup.
questions.why: We avoid carrying known errors into the new system or changing records without an owner.

questions.label: What must stay available during the move?
questions.help: Choose critical services; add acceptable interruption and who can check the result.
questions.why: We plan redirects, continuity, backups, and rollback around these priorities before switching.

modules.title: Measurement and performance

questions.label: Which business or website results do you track today?
questions.help: Choose measures and add a report link or tool name if available.
questions.why: We check what evidence exists before proposing reporting or new tracking.

optionLabels.Conversion: Visits that lead to a purchase or inquiry

questions.label: What starting numbers do you already have for your main goal?
questions.placeholder: For example: Approximately 20 inquiries per month, from our CRM
questions.help: Reuse your earlier baseline; add only new detail with dates and a source.
questions.why: Comparable starting numbers help assess progress; estimates are welcome and revenue is optional.

questions.label: What decisions should your reports help you make?
questions.help: Name the decision, report reader, and useful review frequency.
presets: Help us decide what to measure
questions.why: We focus reporting on actions your team can take, rather than collect metrics without a purpose.

questions.label: Where do people stop before completing a purchase or request?
questions.help: Share a recent step-by-step report or an example; include dates and the source.
questions.why: We use the same period and definitions to locate drop-off. Unknown steps become measurement work, not guessed conversion rates.
questions.placeholder: For example: October store report — 2,000 visits, 90 checkout starts, 30 orders.
presets: We do not track the steps yet

questions.why: We compare requests with the agreed coverage; maintenance and new feature work need clear limits.

questions.label: Which service interruptions would hurt your business most?
questions.help: Choose critical failures; add busy periods and recovery needs if known.
questions.why: These priorities guide a support discussion; they do not create response-time or recovery guarantees.

questions.label: Who should receive alerts and approve maintenance work?
questions.help: Reuse a contact or name a responsible role; add a suitable update window.
questions.why: We need an owner for access, subscriptions, and approval of disruptive or extra work.
